correctness.rationale: After a first force at 0 the blue vertices are N[0] plus d. The only outside vertices adjacent to any member of N[0] are −2, 2, n−1 and n+1. Without one of them blue, no vertex can make a second force. Reflection reduces sufficiency to d=n+1 (two complete consecutive rungs already) or d=2 (vertex 1 forces n+1). Two complete consecutive rungs force the next by the two cycle edges, skipping any targets already blue, so the process finishes. For the orbit step, with blue neighbor pair {−1,1}, d=±2 gives row 1 and d=n±1 gives row 2; with {1,n}, the choices 2,−2,n−1,n+1 give rows 2,3,4,5, and the last neighbor pair is the reflection. Their cyclic gap words are (1,1,1,2n−3), (1,1,n−2,n), (1,2,n−2,n−1), (1,n−2,1,n) and (1,n−1,1,n−1). For n≥4 these are distinct modulo shifts and reversals, with respective dihedral stabilizers 2,1,1,2,4. For n=3, K₃,₃ forces from a four-set exactly when a vertex is omitted on each side, giving nine. The prior scalar result identifies the classified sets as minimum.
residual_risks: The finite computation is corroboration only. The all-order argument is the first-force and cyclic-gap analysis.

originality.rationale: The main exact claim is covered by distinct indexed statements, irrespective of unresolved relative priority. The November five-orbit record explicitly gives the same representatives, sizes and 13n for the entire n≥4 range. The October seven-family record also supplies the same local first-force candidates and resolves rotations into five dihedral classes for n≥6. The n=3 boundary is the immediate complete-bipartite characterization. This verdict concerns demonstrable overlap, not when or by whom either proof was first obtained.
residual_risks: The comparisons establish equivalent mathematical content, not priority or dependence. The distinct records have differing displayed dates; those dates do not establish order of discovery.

value.rationale: A minimum-layer coefficient and a complete orbit table for a cubic family are worthwhile objectives. But the exact family classification is available in the checked records, and the n=3 boundary is immediate from K₃,₃. The frozen record offers no surviving distinct invariant or motivated phenomenon apart from that covered classification; the explicit first-move form is also covered on the arbitrary-order range by the seven-family proof.
residual_risks: The value verdict does not deny the usefulness of the classification itself or decide chronological priority.
